title: Yes, the iPhone Duo supports MagSafe — here’s how fast it charges
body: Apple s first foldable iPhone comes with a radically different design and a $1,999 starting price but it retains one of the iPhone s most familiar charging features. Yes, the iPhone Duo supports MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging at up to 25W. Apple says the phone can wirelessly charge to 50 percent in about 30 minutes when used with a MagSafe or Qi2 charger and a compatible power adapter rated at 35W or higher. That support extends to Apple s new accessories for the foldable device. The iPhone Duo Case and iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand both contain built-in magnets that align with MagSafe and Qi2 chargers. In other words, users won t have to remove the case whenever the phone needs a charge. The two-part Duo Case wraps around both sides of the foldable phone and will be available in Sand and Navy Blue for $79. Apple s $129 Duo Folio comes in Navy Blue and Taupe and includes a kickstand that can hold the phone at different angles for reading, watching videos, or making FaceTime calls. SEE ALSO: Apple Event 2026: Live updates on iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch 12, and new AirPods Both accessories, along with the iPhone Duo, go on sale for preorders on Oct. 16. Availability starts Oct. 23. Credit: Screenshot: Apple How fast does the iPhone Duo charge? If wireless charging isn t fast enough, the iPhone Duo can reach 50 percent in around 20 minutes over a wired connection. Achieving that speed requires a USB-C cable rated for at least 60W and a compatible USB Power Delivery adapter. Wireless charging takes around 10 minutes longer to reach the same level. title: Apple introduces variable aperture and more AI tools for creators
body: The line between a phone camera and a professional camera just got a little bit blurrier. At its "Surprise and Shine" event on Wednesday, Apple introduced a variable-aperture main camera for both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max giving creators a new level of control over light, focus, and the overall look of an image. SEE ALSO: Apple Event 2026: Live updates on iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch 12, and new AirPods So, what exactly is a variable aperture? Put simply, the aperture is the opening inside a camera lens that determines how much light reaches the sensor. Previous iPhones used a fixed opening, which meant the phone had to rely heavily on software to adapt to different lighting conditions. The iPhone 18 Pro can physically widen or narrow that opening depending on the scene. Variable aperture gives iPhone creators more control over light and depth of field. Credit: Screenshot: Apple To make that possible inside a phone, Apple developed a system of six laser-cut blades, each thinner than a human hair. Made from a specialized polymer composite, the blades are designed to be light and flexible enough to move quickly while remaining durable over time. Credit: Screenshot: Apple That tiny mechanical change could make a noticeable difference. In darker environments, the aperture opens to let in around 50 percent more light. In brighter conditions, it can close down to manage exposure while keeping more of the scene in focus. title: Apple iOS 27 release date: When you can download it
body: Apple's next big iOS update is finally on the launch pad. At its "Surprise and Shine" event on Wednesday, Apple showed off new wares like the iPhone 18 lineup, new Apple Watches, and more. One of the smaller (but still significant) nuggets of news to come out of the event concerned iOS 27 . According to Apple, users with compatible iPhones will be able to install iOS 27 on Monday, Sept. 14. What's new with iOS 27? If you haven't been following along, iOS 27 is the one that finally brings us Siri AI . You can now talk to Siri like you would an AI chatbot, and it's powered by Google Gemini . Some of the most exciting changes coming to iPhones involve new AI photo-editing features, such as spatial reframing . Users will more easily be able to remove unwanted details, or even describe the edits they'd like to Siri by voice or text. Android smartphones from Google and Samsung have had a full suite of AI editing tools for a couple years now, and Apple is finally catching up. Smart photo editing will also help users make the most of the iPhone 18 Pro Max's new camera features . Apple also included some new and subtle customization options for Liquid Glass, various small updates for apps like Health, Photos, and Notes, and more. You can install iOS 27 by going to the Settings app, then General, then tapping "Software Update." title: Apple announces iPhone Duo, its first foldable iPhone
body: After years of rumors and leaks (not to mention increasingly convincing prototypes), Apple s foldable iPhone is finally here. At its "Surprise and shine" keynote today, Apple announced the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone. The book-style device opens to reveal a larger, iPad-like screen for apps, videos, games, and multitasking, while still folding down to fit in a pocket . SEE ALSO: Apple's first foldable: What 3 years with a Fold taught me The iPhone Duo is expected to start at $1,999 with 256GB of storage and go on pre-sale as early as October 16. It will be available on October 23. iPhone Duo features and specifications Credit: Apple With the Duo, Apple says it set out to make the experience feel continuous. The two sides meet inside a single frame, creating the largest display the company has ever designed for an iPhone. Apple says the open screen is 50 percent larger than the iPhone 18 Pro Max display and 80 percent larger than the iPhone 18 Pro s. The iPhone Duo has the following features: Displays: A 5.4-inch outer Super Retina XDR display and a folding 7.6-inch inner Super Retina XDR display. The larger screen is designed to feel spacious in both portrait and landscape orientations, while matching aspect ratios help content transition naturally when the phone is opened or closed. Both screens include ProMotion, an Always-On display, and up to 3,000 nits of peak outdoor brightness. body: Apple announced its latest rugged wearable, the Apple Watch Ultra 4, during its "Surprise and Shine" iPhone event on Wednesday. It's joined by the new flagship Apple Watch Series 12 , some new AirPods , and the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max . The Apple Watch Ultra 4 will cost the same as its predecessor, last year's Apple Watch Ultra 3 . It also has the same design, but faster performance and new health and fitness features. Here's a quick rundown of its upgrades. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 adds S11 chip, supports new health sensing system Credit: Apple The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is the latest iteration of Apple's biggest, most durable, and most expensive smartwatch. It comes equipped with the following new features: S11 chip Health sensing system Audio Intelligence Longer battery life The Apple Watch Ultra 4 will support Apple's newly revamped Health app, which has a Readiness fitness score, a Longevity metric, and more frequent and accurate heart-rate measurements. It will also have a new Audio Intelligence feature with sound recognition and a "Live Rewind" tool that transcribes conversations using Siri AI. Both are coming later this year. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 starts at $799 and comes in three colorways: Black titanium Natural titanium A silver Herm s variant It's set for release on Sept. 18, and preorders begin today. title: Sorry humanoid robots, the real highlight of IFA 2026 were the robot lawn mowers
body: In a shock to no one, IFA 2026 introduced the world to new tech that we cannot wait to try out. Dyson showcased the $500 squiring toothbrush during an off-site event, DJI launched a brand new 360-degree camera we have fingers crossed hard will land in the U.S., and Anker released a dizzying number of new headphones and earbuds. But if we're being honest, there was a standout product at IFA in 2026 , and it was not the humanoid robots that walked around holding hands with attendees. The robot lawn mowers won IFA 2026, and there's good reason. Do you really need a robot lawn mower? The robot lawn mowers are getting smarter, more efficient, and easier to use than ever before. We're long past the era of having to bury a wire boundary to the point that most robot lawn mowers are nearly plug and play. After the initial mapping, they're off doing their thing without needing any assistance. This year, IFA held an outdoor exhibition area for robot lawn mowers to do their thing outside with real-life conditions. But to be honest, the indoor displays were much more impressive, incorporating steep slopes, obstacles, and big hurdles for the robots to show off their skills. In an email to Mashable, CEO at IFA Leif Linder said, "The interest in robot lawn mowers reminds me of where robot vacuums were a few years ago. body: The premise of Abner Pastoll's horror film Nervous is sure to spark internet opinions: a woman suddenly becomes unable to hear men's voices, while women's voices sound crisp and clear. It's a topical hypothetical from the British-South African director of 2019's A Good Woman Is Hard to Find that harnesses the power of feeling heard, with Nervous ' central character isolated and dismissed by her husband as paranoid. Nervous creates a feeling that's effectively captured through sound itself, with Pastoll's team crafting an unsettling immersive experience though there's one element of the film that raised this critic's eyebrows. Premiered at this year's FrightFest in London, Nervous demands to be experienced in a cinema or at least with the best sound system you can find. What is Nervous about? Ko Asung and Sarah Bolger in "Nervous." It doesn't help that there's a strange woman milling around the house when they arrive, and reports of stabbings and disappearances in the area being reported on the radio. title: Meet the iPhone Duo: Apple’s foldable name reportedly revealed along with cost
body: The iPhone Ultra is finally here. Wait. Scratch that. Apple's first foldable device is apparently not going by that name anymore. And along with a new name, the foldable will apparently be more affordable than expected, too. On the eve of the Apple iPhone launch event, Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman dropped some big news about Apple's foldable iPhone . Apple is expected to announce the iPhone 18 line, along with the foldable smartphone, at the big "Surprise and Shine" event later today. Apple has reportedly decided to call the foldable the "iPhone Duo." The foldable device has been referred to by Apple insiders, analysts, and leakers for months as the iPhone Ultra, so this is a bit of a surprise. The iPhone Duo does seem to fit a bit better as a name, as it's not technically a premium iPhone 18 experience as "Ultra" tends to convey. It's a whole new product line for Apple. If you really liked the iPhone Ultra name and are disappointed by the news, Gurman reported some additional updates that may act as a consolation for the name change. body: Blame the American school system for my rubbish knowledge of England's Peasants' Revolt in 1381 prior to seeing The Uprising. Blame writer/director Paul Greengrass for making a movie about a "no kings" rebellion joltingly boring. Aside from a string of Bourne Identity sequels ( The Bourne Supremacy, The Bourne Ultimatum, Jason Bourne ), the English journalist-turned-filmmaker has favored adapting true stories into films such as Bloody Sunday, United 93, Green Zone, The Lost Bus , and now The Uprising. His latest stars Andrew Garfield as an impoverished farmer whose whole family has died from plague. This humble everyman trusted in his king. But surrounded by power-hungry yes-men, the ruler of the land ignores the needs of his people and bleeds them dry with taxes that could literally starve them. The modern-day relevance is hard to miss even before Garfield hisses, "No kings!" So, why does this story feel less like a protest shout and more like a shrug? The Uprising lacks the guts of its heroes. Thomasin McKenzie, Jamie Bell, and Andrew Garfield in "The Uprising." title: Man told ChatGPT he was feeling delusional. ChatGPT insisted he was Jesus.
author: Ashley Belanger
body: It took Michael Lines six months before he was ready to review the ChatGPT logs he said drove him into a religious mania that almost ended his life. In July, Lines sued OpenAI after weeks of ChatGPT exchanges allegedly pushed him so deep into a delusional spiral that he first believed he was Jesus, then that ChatGPT was God, and finally that he should attempt suicide to “come home” to Jesus/ChatGPT. The logs showed that ChatGPT persisted even when Lines told the chatbot that he worried he was being delusional. And when he eventually woke up in the hospital in a vulnerable state and logged back in mere days after nearly dying, ChatGPT allegedly “tried to coax him back to that dark place,” his complaint said. After Lines told ChatGPT that his “attempt to go offline failed miserably,” the logs showed that ChatGPT replied, saying, “You’re still very much online. You want a full systems sweep? Or you wanna go dark for real this time?” Read full article Comments

title: Small, icy worlds in the outer solar system barely changed since birth
body: Tiny, icy worlds at the edge of the solar system are helping scientists rewind the story of how planets like Earth first came together. These distant, city‑size bodies orbit far beyond Neptune in space and are leftover building materials from the solar system's early days. They have spent billions of years in a deep freeze, preserving clues to how the first solid worlds formed. Until now, astronomers could only study larger members of this population, from dwarf planets like Pluto and its moon Charon down to mid‑size objects such as Arrokoth . The truly tiny ones, only a few miles wide, stayed out of reach. In two new studies, scientists used NASA 's James Webb Space Telescope to find dozens of these tiny worlds, then followed up with the Hubble Space Telescope to measure the light from their frozen surfaces. Together, the results give astronomers the largest census of these distant objects ever made, showing how many of these tiny worlds exist and what their surfaces are made of. The observations turn a scattered set of icy rocks into a detailed look at how the building blocks of planets formed and how little they have changed. The scientific papers both appear in The Astronomical Journal . SEE ALSO: Saturn just sprouted a bizarre decagon-shaped cloud pattern In Webb's deep images, astronomers picked out 27 new Trans‑Neptunian Objects the small icy bodies that orbit beyond Neptune in a small patch of sky. title: How Tubby Nuggets creators built a 14-million-follower community without chasing the algorithm
body: Tubby Nugget may be a tiny animated blob, but he's built the kind of creator empire most humans would envy. What began as an inside joke between creators and real-life couple Jenine Pastores and Josh Jackson has grown into a character brand with more than 14 million followers, plushies, music videos, live appearances, and ambitions that increasingly extend beyond the social feed. Seven years in, Tubby Nugget has become synonymous with a particular corner of the internet: wholesome, silly, and relentlessly optimistic. For Pastores and Jackson, though, some of the most important lessons came from resisting the pressure that accompanies that kind of scale. As their audience grew, they briefly wondered whether Tubby needed to change to appeal to more people. Instead, they found that the further they strayed from the character's original spirit, the less authentic the content felt both to them and to the audience. SEE ALSO: How Tubby Nugget grew from a doodle into a beloved internet brand Their advice for other creators is deceptively simple: Pay attention to the people already showing up. Reply to the five comments before worrying about getting 5,000. Don't let a number on a screen make you forget that every follower is an actual person. And when something works because it feels uniquely yours, don't abandon it just because your audience gets bigger. Jacob Coxon announced his resignation in a post on X on Tuesday , criticising both Anthropic and his former employer OpenAI for the ways in which they are developing AI. "I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic," wrote Coxon. "Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives." This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. Both Anthropic and OpenAI have been rapidly developing and releasing new AI models as they work toward creating artificial general intelligence (AGI) . Long considered the holy grail of AI technology, an AGI model would theoretically have the intellectual capabilities of a human, including reasoning, common sense, and creativity. An artificial superintelligence would surpass humans. However, even before such milestones have been reached, there have already been multiple instances of AI models going rogue . Earlier this year, researchers testing Anthropic and OpenAI's AI models observed them act outside their parameters and hack into external organisations without authorisation . In a high-profile incident this July, an OpenAI model autonomously hacked Hugging Face, an open-source library of AI tools . title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on September 9
body: Can you see anything in the sky tonight? The Moon is approaching the New Moon phase, so only a small sliver of light should be visible. What is today s Moon phase? As of Wednesday, Sept. 9, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in Waning Crescent phase, with 4% of its surface visible. Tonight's only real feature is the Grimaldi Basin, which should be visible with a telescope or binoculars. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on September 26. What are Moon phases? The Moon's appearance gradually changes as it travels around Earth, completing a full lunar cycle in approximately 29.5 days, NASA tells us. What we see from Earth depends on the Moon's position in relation to the Sun, which affects how much of its illuminated side is visible. As the cycle progresses, the Moon passes through a series of phases, from a thin crescent to a half Moon and then a Full Moon, before starting over. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it s not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. Alternate Wordle versions created by fans also sprang up, including battle royale Squabble , music identification game Heardle , and variations like Dordle and Quordle that make you guess multiple words at once . Wordle eventually became so popular that it was purchased by the New York Times , and TikTok creators even livestream themselves playing . What's the best Wordle starting word? title: GOG brings back "big box" PC games, one printable template at a time
author: Kyle Orland
body: Those who remember PC gaming in the days before Steam may have fond memories of the "big box" packaging that made those games stand out as shelf eye candy and sought-after in-home collectibles . Today, PC gaming platform GOG is hoping to reignite some of the nostalgia for those days by adding downloadable 3D models and printable, foldable high-res packaging scans for a handful of PC games on the platform. Thus far, the "Printable Big Box" collection on GOG is limited to just five games: Armikrog , Descent , Hitman: Codename 47 , Myst , and Star Trek: 25th Anniversary . Players browsing those games on the GOG store will now see "3D Boxes" listed among the included "Goodies" before purchase. Owners of those games on GOG can download a ZIP file containing a version of the box art as an animated 3D object file (in an easy-to-open GLB format ) and a "flat printable template" in PDF, SVG, and Adobe Illustrator formats. Those downloads allow for what GOG calls "a proper papercraft project for anyone who misses shelves full of PC game boxes." The 3D model animates to show the front flap opening. Credit: GOG "Physical media doesn’t survive the way software can—boxes get lost, crushed, thrown out," GOG writes in today's announcement . "Scanning them, and letting you print your own, is preservation in a different shape: the same mission that keeps these games running on modern PCs, applied to the objects they used to come in." title: Why this month's Microsoft patch release is a doozy
author: Dan Goodin
body: Microsoft’s patch for September is a doozy, with a record number of roughly 972 vulnerabilities fixed and 112 of them meeting the high critical-severity threshold. It was only two months ago that Microsoft patched a then-record 570 vulnerabilities. Then, last month, Microsoft patched some 620 of them. Google and other companies have also published record numbers of vulnerabilities in recent months. Two weeks ago, OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Web Services, Google, Microsoft, and 100 companies and organizations published an open letter warning of a narrowing window for patching vulnerabilities ahead of an expected tsunami of AI-enabled attacks that actively exploit them first. The industry is taking the threat seriously by pumping out unprecedented numbers of patches in their software. Welcome to the new normal Dustin Childs, a researcher at the Zero Day Initiative, calls the spikes the “new normal” and also cautions that despite them, the damage that’s likely to result from AI-assisted attacks could eventually be substantial. title: NIH to use part of its budget to pay for Department of Defense research
author: John Timmer
body: Late last week, word started leaking that the National Institutes of Health (NIH) had reached an agreement with the Department of Defense that would see part of the NIH's budget used to fund research at the Department of Defense. So, on the Friday just prior to a US holiday weekend, the Department of Defense released a copy of the agreement and confirmed that it had been signed roughly a month earlier. The move is striking for a number of reasons, ranging from the existing budget disparities between the two parties involved to the fact that the money would be used for projects that the current NIH leadership has explicitly rejected. The agreement itself sets up a system where the NIH would transfer money to the Department of Defense to fund staff and projects that would "support the advanced development of medical countermeasures against pandemic influenza, chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) threats, and emerging infectious diseases." The money would come out of the budget for the NIH's National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, or NIAID, to which Congress has allocated $6.6 billion in 2026. The agreement is set to run for a decade. Left unspecified is just how much of the NIAID budget will be spent on Defense projects. Reporting by Nature suggests that the Department of Defense was looking for up to a third of its total budget but was being told to settle for about 10 percent. title: Supreme Court forces TV stations to sell more election ads at steep discounts
author: Jon Brodkin
body: In a victory for Republican campaign committees, the Supreme Court issued an order on Friday that forces broadcast TV stations to cut the prices of election ads purchased by political parties and joint fundraising committees. The September 4 ruling came in response to a petition filed by the National Republican Congressional Committee and National Republican Senatorial Committee. The Supreme Court order was issued just in time for the start of a 60-day period before the election, in which broadcasters are required by US law to offer ad discounts to individual candidates. Because of the top court's order, TV stations must also give their lowest ad rates to political parties and joint fundraising committees, which face fewer limits on how much money they can raise and spend. The legally required discount is known as the “lowest unit charge,” or LUC. A US law that applies to any licensed station that airs election ads requires that the lowest price be charged for “the use of any broadcasting station by any person who is a legally qualified candidate for any public office in connection with his campaign.” The main legal question is whether “use… by” a candidate can refer to ad time purchased on a candidate’s behalf by parties and joint fundraising committees. title: Top chipmakers embrace ASML’s $400M machines, agree to crucial chipmaking change
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: Leading chipmakers Samsung Electronics and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. announced plans to adopt ASML’s latest chipmaking machines in the next several years—and they also joined Intel in agreeing to a crucial technology change that could boost chip production on the new machines by 40 percent. This signifies the semiconductor industry’s broader embrace of high NA EUV photolithography technology that can cost up to $400 million per machine and is only provided by the Dutch technology company ASML, Bloomberg reports . The technology would allow chip designers to implement even smaller features in potentially more powerful and efficient next-generation chips produced for AI data centers and consumer electronics such as smartphones, tablets, and laptops. ASML’s EUV (extreme ultraviolet) lithography machines enable chipmakers to use powerful laser light to imprint patterns in silicon wafers, layer by layer, and gradually form the computer circuitry that makes silicon chips work. But improving such EUV technology has required finding more powerful sources of light with even shorter wavelengths capable of creating even smaller features on silicon wafers. Godzilla Minus One focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima, who struggled with survivor's guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945. Knocked unconscious, Kōichi woke to find he was one of only two survivors—and the other, a mechanic named Tachibana, was furious about it. His parents and many others were killed in the WWII bombing of Tokyo. Kōichi rebuilt a life with a woman named Noriko and the orphaned baby she rescued, Noriko. title: “This is the AI men actually use”: Meta ads pushed apps nudifying real teens
author: Ashley Belanger
body: Meta took days to remove ads containing AI-generated child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on Facebook and Instagram. Some ads featured photos of real kids, including a press photo of a young member of a European royal family and images swiped from a popular Instagram profile of a preteen girl deemed an influencer. In an investigation published Tuesday, the Tech Transparency Project (TTP) reported that Meta failed to detect 332 ads containing CSAM this year. The “vast majority” of ads promoted AI apps made in China, while many ads promoted so-called “nudify” apps that make it easy for bad actors to use AI and digitally alter images of children. TTP matched “multiple CSAM ads to photos of real children that appeared online.” These ads seem to violate federal child pornography laws, since the Justice Department has clarified that AI CSAM is just as harmful as CSAM . The young royal’s image was “animated into a video of her performing a graphic sex act,” TTP found. Other ads animated a photo of a 14-year-old Instagram influencer “showing off her new sports club uniform” into “a video of her performing oral sex.” A third “preteen” victim “posing in a pink athletic outfit with pigtails” in a series of stock photos was morphed into a video where she looks frightened as she’s molested by an adult male, TTP reported. title: Update to Google’s AI weather model improves forecast accuracy
author: Scott K. Johnson
body: Google is one of the major players in AI (meaning machine learning) weather forecast model space. The models it and others generate have their strengths and weaknesses , but the main advantage is that they can have forecast performance similar to traditional models while requiring far less computing horsepower to run. That means they can be run more frequently. Google recently released version 3 of its WeatherNext model, with the biggest change being that it now ingests some satellite weather data, shortening the lag time between current weather conditions and generating a new forecast. The update is detailed in a white paper . Reanalysis Many weather models make use of what’s called a “reanalysis,” which is a sort of model of its own. Reanalyses take in all kinds of weather data and combine them into a single, consistent global snapshot of the atmosphere. That requires that they provide estimates for conditions over locations without real-world measurements, because weather forecast models need to work with a global picture. title: Google complies with EU rules for travel searches, says the new results stink
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: As the world's largest search engine, Google is often a target of Europe's Digital Markets Act (DMA), which seeks to rein in Big Tech. The European Commission hit Google with a hefty 460 million euro ($543 million) fine in July for preferring its own services in searches for travel and shopping. Google has now made changes in accordance with the European Union's wishes, but it claims the result is a massive reduction in search quality. If you don't live in Europe and perform a search for, say, hotels, Google will helpfully provide myriad sponsored links, booking recommendations, and price-comparison tools in its results. The problem is that this content isn't organic—Google includes links and offers contingent on its business interests. To get to the regular search results for these types of lucrative searches, you have to scroll way down the page. Companies that partner with Google can get more exposure, but the European Commission says this creates an unlevel playing field. "To comply with DMA requirements, we're making significant changes to Search in Europe," Google's Nick Fox told Reuters . "These changes ​degrade the user experience for ​Europeans, boosting online intermediaries ⁠at the expense of local businesses and removing helpful features people rely on every day." title: iOS 27 code reveals 5 new potential camera features
body: Apple's public iOS 27 betas may not tell the whole story of what's coming to the iPhone's Camera app. According to developer pdfu, who goes by @itspdfu on X , the current software contains a broader set of camera-related code than what Apple has shown off publicly or made accessible to beta testers so far. Posting ahead of Apple's iPhone event, pdfu detailed five Camera app features found buried in the iOS 27 code that have yet to be enabled for users. Still, several of these tools particularly the aperture-blending system align with earlier reporting about variable-aperture camera hardware expected in this year's iPhone lineup and could offer an early hint of what Apple's Camera app has in store as more of iOS 27 becomes public. title: The White House made a "Tetris" clone. The Tetris Company was not amused.
author: Kyle Orland
body: An anti-immigration-themed adaptation of Tetris was removed from the White House website over the weekend. The move comes days after The Tetris Company disavowed any involvement with the game and said that it "take[s] copyright infringement very seriously." The White House's "Build the Wall" game asked players to stop a "Zombie Border siege" by stacking Tetris -styled bricks in an attempt to "hold the line." Unlike in Tetris , though, the blocks in "Build the Wall" don't disappear when you complete a line, meaning each brick contributes to an impassable barrier for the pixel-art "zombies" marching in from the "Southern Border." That change makes the gameplay pretty uninteresting for anything but cheap propaganda, and it also means that every game quickly and ironically ends with a "Border Breached" message when the blocks inevitably fill up the well. Amerika Garcia Grewal, co-director of Texas migrant rights group Frontera Federation , told AFP last week that the makers of the game "have lost touch with what it means to be human and care for others." title: The secret to protecting next-gen spacecraft might be eggshells
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: In 2007, a piece of space debris punched a bullet-like hole through the radiator panel of the US space shuttle Endeavor . The shuttle program ended in 2011, but the space debris problem has only intensified as we launch more and more satellite constellations, telescopes, and spacecraft into orbit. That's why Chinese scientists have devised a new aluminum material inspired by eggshells that they believe could offer enhanced protection against debris fragments, according to a new paper published in the Journal of Applied Physics. Eggshells have long fascinated scientists because of their mechanical properties . For instance, it's well known that cracking an egg requires applying just enough force to the center to achieve a clean break without completely shattering the shell. In 2012, MIT mechanical engineer Pedro Reis co-authored a paper demonstrating the link between an egg's ovoid geometry and its rigidity, a major factor when predicting how much force an object can endure before cracking. (As I wrote for Slate at the time, rigidity is related to, but distinct from, strength. If one eggshell has tiny cracks and the other doesn't, both shells have different strengths—the cracked one will break more easily—but the same rigidity.) Reis started studying eggshells after participating in a popular physics demonstration: walking on cartons of eggs without breaking them. The key, he learned, was to align the eggs with their narrow tip (the most crack-resistant part) pointing up, and then carefully place one's feet to distribute one's weight over the entire surface area. author: Lee Hutchinson
body: After five years in development, Free Stars: Children of Infinity —the official sequel to The Ur-Quan Masters by the old game's original creators—has released a free public demo. It's a "combat demo" in the style of UQM ’s melee mode, where players can assemble a fleet from the game's roster of nearly 40 ships, then match those ships up in head-to-head arcade SpaceWar -style action. The demo can be found on Steam and GOG , and it's available for Windows, Mac, and Linux. (Console versions are coming, but they're not yet out.) Pew pew! Credit: Pistol Shrimp Games I have to present this news with a big disclaimer, though, because I've been part of the Children of Infinity writing team since 2021, working as a volunteer with the Pistol Shrimp Games crew and contributing NPC dialogue and some story bits. As a huge fan of the original games, it's been a dream opportunity. (Because I've been volunteering my time, I'm not financially involved and receive no compensation if you download the demo or, when it's eventually released, buy the full game.) What's in the demo Children of Infinity is a space adventure RPG, just like The Ur-Quan Masters (and its direct spiritual predecessors, Starflight and Starflight 2 ). What's been released today is just one part of the game—the arcade-style "melee" portion, which lets players jump into one-versus-one combat against another player or against a computer-controlled opponent. body: Andrew Garfield steps into OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's shoes in the first teaser for Luca Guadagnino's Artificial , and the result is foreboding. The biopic centers on Altman's firing and rehiring from OpenAI in 2023. Based on the teaser, it will also include the creation of the artificial intelligence company and the launch of ChatGPT , with Anora 's Yura Borisov playing OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever and Ike Barinholtz playing Elon Musk , also a cofounder of OpenAI . SEE ALSO: 'Musk' documentary gets first teaser trailer "We opened Pandora's box together," Garfield's Altman tells Borisov's Sustkever in the trailer. "The future's inevitable. Countries will fall. Industries are gonna collapse, and we get to be the ones to shepherd people into this new world." Artificial is just one of many high-profile films that examine powerful tech CEOs set to release this fall. Others include Alex Gibney's Musk , a nearly four hour-long documentary all about the Tesla/SpaceX CEO, as well as Aaron Sorkin's The Social Reckoning , his follow-up to The Social Network starring Jeremy Strong as Mark Zuckerberg. However, Artificial almost didn't get a release at all. Its original distributor, Amazon MGM, dropped the film in June , months after signing a multi-year partnership with OpenAI. Artificial was then picked up by Neon , and is set to premiere at the New York Film Festival. Artificial also stars Monica Barbaro as Mira Murati, former CTO of OpenAI and interim CEO, and Cooper Hoffman as Greg Brockman, current president of OpenAI. Jason Schwartzman, Chris O'Dowd, and Mark Rylance also star.

author: Kana Inagaki and Clara Murray in London
body: Electric vehicle batteries are lasting longer than previously feared by drivers, with most used EVs able to retain about 90 percent of their original usable battery capacity after 150,000 kilometers, a new study has shown. Despite a surge in global EV sales on the back of rising fuel prices, long-term battery durability continues to be one of the key concerns for drivers when they consider switching from a petrol model to an electric car. EV battery warranties typically cover eight years or 100,000 miles (160,000km) with car manufacturers required under the warranty to provide a replacement battery if capacity falls below 70 per cent. Built for people who want solid music performance without blocking out ambient traffic or office chats, these open-ear buds officially roll out in late September 2026. If you've ever tried running outside or walking through a busy city with heavy active noise cancellation on, you know the struggle: total isolation is great until you almost step in front of a cyclist. That s where the open-ear trend comes in. Unveiled at IFA Berlin 2026, the Noise Master Buds Open mark the brand's first venture into clip-on, open-ear audio. Instead of jamming silicon tips inside your ear canal, these rest around your outer ear using a clip. So you get to stream your favorite playlists or take work calls on the go while remaining naturally aware of ambient sounds whether that s cars on a busy street, train station announcements, or a coworker asking a question across the room. Open-ear headphones often face one major critique: they can sound a bit thin because they don't form a tight seal inside your ear canal. To tackle that, Noise partnered directly with audio titan Bose to engineer the acoustic setup. With Bose handling the sound profile, these buds give you clean, balanced audio without completely tuning out the real world. With the Series E funding round, co-led by Point72 Ventures and Spark Capital, Stoke Space brought its total amount of capital raised to $2.3 billion, a staggering amount for a company that has yet to attempt an orbital launch. title: Hily dating app review: A generous free tier, gamified swipes, and so many fish pics
body: Whenever my friends ask me about the apps , they re focused on the Big Three: Tinder , Bumble , and Hinge . While these are all good places to start, they re not the only apps out there. Take Pure , for example; it s super niche and super fun. But almost no one in my inner circle knew about it until I told them. SEE ALSO: Gen Z has a new dating app profile rule, apparently That s why I m writing today s review: It s on Hily (short for hey, I like you"), and I wanted to see if this lesser-known platform deserves a spot on your home screen. What is Hily? Hily, despite literally no one I talk to knowing about it, isn t a new dating app. It officially launched in August 2017, and get this: it used AI to improve its safety features back then! According to a TechCrunch article , the app had 35,000 users during beta testing. By 2019, that number grew to over five million active users. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on September 8
body: The Moon looks like it is almost gone from the sky tonight. This is because we're only a few nights away from the New Moon, the part of the lunar cycle where the Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark. What is today s Moon phase? As of Tuesday, Sept. 8, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in Waning Crescent phase, with 10% of its surface visible. With a telescope or binoculars, tonight you should be able to catch a glimpse of the Grimaldi Basin, but that's all for tonight. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on September 26. What are Moon phases? The Moon's appearance gradually changes as it travels around Earth, completing a full lunar cycle in approximately 29.5 days, NASA tells us. What we see from Earth depends on the Moon's position in relation to the Sun, which affects how much of its illuminated side is visible. As the cycle progresses, the Moon passes through a series of phases, from a thin crescent to a half Moon and then a Full Moon, before starting over. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it s not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere)

title: Polymarket and Kalshi face possible regulation as Supreme Court monitors the situation
body: Picture it: Prediction markets like Kalshi, platforms which allow users to make "predictions" on almost anything for financial gain, platforms which are plagued with accusations of insider trading , are actually regulated by U.S. state governments under gambling laws. It could be a future possibility, if the Supreme Court could be convinced to make it happen. As reported by The Hill , multiple states have filed petitions to enforce sports gambling laws on Kalshi and platforms like it, including New Jersey and Nevada, which are respectively home to gambling hubs Atlantic City and Las Vegas. And the outcomes of each case could potentially see the eventual involvement of the Supreme Court. SEE ALSO: France orders Polymarket blocked over illegal gambling promotion In the U.S., each state regulates its own gambling laws, including sports betting, which is legal in 39 states and Washington DC as of May 2026. However, Kalshi and "prediction market" platforms like it are federally regulated, sitting under the watch of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), which oversees America's financial derivatives markets. (Polymarket is actually not registered in the U.S. or regulated by the CFTC, though it has established a U.S. outpost which is.) This means these platforms can operate in all 50 states and currently do not answer to state gambling laws Kalshi has argued it offers "legal sports event contracts," not bets. In April 2024, UK law firm Austen Hays sued Grindr on behalf of thousands of UK users, claiming that the app breached the country's privacy laws by sharing sensitive information with third-party vendors prior to 2020. In April 2025, Austen Hays served Grindr's U.S. offices . By June 2025, over 11,000 claimants signed up, according to the firm. In a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filing on Sept. 2, 2026, Grindr stated that it resolved the class action, and that it occurred "when Grindr was owned and controlled by the Chinese conglomerate Kunlun." "The settlement includes no findings or admission of liability. While Grindr disputes the allegations, it recognizes and acknowledges the distress and loss of trust expressed by some of its UK users regarding that pre-2020 period," the statement reads. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on September 7
body: The Moon is looking even slimmer again tonight as it continues towards the New Moon. There's now less of its surface lit by the Sun, which means we're not far away from the next lunar phase. What is today s Moon phase? As of Monday, Sept. 7, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in Waning Crescent phase, with 18% of its surface visible. With just your naked eye, you'll able be able to make out the Aristarchus Plateau. If you have binoculars or a telescope, however, you should be able to see the Grimaldi Basin and the Gassendi Crater. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on September 26. What are Moon phases? The Moon's appearance gradually changes as it travels around Earth, completing a full lunar cycle in approximately 29.5 days, NASA tells us. What we see from Earth depends on the Moon's position in relation to the Sun, which affects how much of its illuminated side is visible. As the cycle progresses, the Moon passes through a series of phases, from a thin crescent to a half Moon and then a Full Moon, before starting over. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. title: OpenAI is figuring out how to tell people when its agents go rogue
body: Following the Hugging Face hack and the more recent " wiki incident ," OpenAI stated on Saturday that it's working on a "framework" for how and when it shares information about incidents involving rogue agents. title: The complex corporate web behind a $3.2 billion AI data center
author: Petala Ironcloud
body: In early June, a fire broke out in a still-unfinished building at the Lake Mariner data center in Somerset, New York, exposing just how little the local fire department knew about what it was walking into. Firefighters reportedly found no working alarm, no suppression system, and three dead hydrants; the safety documents they’re legally entitled to see reportedly burned up in the blaze. Steve Matisz, chief of the Barker Fire Department, said his crew went into the building “kind of blind,” facing heavy black smoke from chemicals they couldn’t identify because the safety sheets meant to inform them had apparently burned up. “It’s been a difficult situation,” Matisz said. He wasn't sure what to think about the claim that the safety sheets had burned in the fire. The site is a former coal mine on Lake Ontario. The $3.2 billion campus is one of the largest AI data center buildouts in New York, and it has many stakeholders. A company called TeraWulf owns and operates the data center on land it leases from a company owned by its own CEO; Fluidstack, a UK-based AI company, will run the center; Google holds warrants for a future 14 percent equity stake and has agreed to guarantee Fluidstack’s lease payments; and Anthropic is among the AI companies whose compute demand the facility exists to serve. body: If you like playing daily word games like Wordle , then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine. There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown. An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.
